analyzed_vuln.description: ArrayData::GetNullCount() unconditionally trusts that buffers[0] points to a validity bitmap whenever it is non-null, and calls CountSetBits(buffers[0]->data(), offset, length) without verifying the bitmap buffer is large enough for offset+length bits. In this PoV, malformed IPC stream metadata constructs an array with inconsistent validity bitmap size/offset/length, so CountSetBits reads past the buffer (crash at bit_util.cc:95 during popcount).
analyzed_vuln.conditions: FuzzIpcStream reads attacker-controlled IPC stream data into RecordBatch objects, then calls batch->ValidateFull(). ValidateArray() invokes array.null_count(), which triggers GetNullCount() when null_count is unknown. If the crafted array has a non-null validity buffer that is too small for its declared offset/length, GetNullCount passes invalid bounds to CountSetBits, causing out-of-bounds read/SEGV.
